FIELD REFERENCE

Rainbow bass (guapote): identity, size and trip checks

For a Central American freshwater trip, rainbow bass means Parachromis dovii, a cichlid also called guapote or guapote lagunero. It is different from peacock bass and the marine rainbow basslet. Confirm the scientific name and water before booking: the same English name can point to a very different fish and trip.

Compare peacock bass, check the Costa Rica fishing card, then choose a lake trip.

Updated 2026-11-24 · Castward

Which fish does rainbow bass mean?

Key factDetail
Freshwater rainbow bassParachromis dovii; family Cichlidae — FishBase
Local namesGuapote lagunero, guapote azul and guapote morrudo — CRAFF-ACPM
Published maximum72 cm total length; 6.8 kg maximum published weight — FishBase
Freshwater habitatLakes and lower or middle river valleys — FishBase
Native rangeCentral America, from named Honduras rivers to named Costa Rica rivers — FishBase
Marine name collisionLiopropoma fasciatum, rainbow basslet: rocky and coral reefs; to 26.5 cm — Smithsonian
Current local bag limitNot stated in these species profiles; check the authority for the exact water
Source check2026-11-24

Is rainbow bass the same as peacock bass?

No. This page covers Parachromis dovii. CRAFF-ACPM identifies it as guapote lagunero and rainbow bass. Do not choose a destination from the English word bass alone. Ask the operator to write the scientific name in the trip details, then match it to the species and water you want to fish.

Read the source

Can rainbow bass also mean a saltwater fish?

Yes. The Smithsonian uses rainbow bass and rainbow basslet for Liopropoma fasciatum, a marine reef fish. Its profile lists a maximum length of 26.5 cm and a range from the central Gulf of California to Ecuador and several offshore islands. That is not the freshwater guapote described on this page.

Read the source

How big do freshwater rainbow bass get?

FishBase lists 72 cm total length and 6.8 kg as published maxima for Parachromis dovii. Those values are size references, not an expected catch. For a trip, ask about the water and method before comparing trophy claims. Keep a maximum-size figure separate from an independently confirmed current world record.

Read the source

What must you check before a Costa Rica fishing trip?

INCOPESCA states that people who fish in marine or inland waters must carry the appropriate fishing card. Check the card category and dates before departure. Ask who arranges your card, whether the planned water needs separate permission, and what happens if conditions change. Do not assume the boat price includes every permission.

Read the source

Are rainbow bass good to eat?

FishBase records food use of Parachromis dovii, including fillets and baked fish. That does not establish permission to keep one from a particular lake. Before you retain a fish, check the local rule and any water-specific consumption advice. Tell the operator beforehand if you prefer to release your catch.

Read the source

What should you know about rainbow bass?

What is the scientific name of guapote lagunero?

Parachromis dovii. CRAFF-ACPM lists rainbow bass among its English names.

Is rainbow bass a cichlid?

Yes. FishBase places Parachromis dovii in the cichlid family.

Does it live in freshwater?

Parachromis dovii lives in freshwater. The marine rainbow basslet is a different fish.

Is 6.8 kg an average catch?

No. FishBase lists that figure as a maximum published weight.

Is there one legal size across Central America?

The species sources do not state one. Use the rules for the country and exact water.

What month should I book?

These sources do not give one fishing peak for every water. Choose the water first and check local conditions for your travel month.
